topics.title: Food
topics.short: Your stock is the food value of every edible item. Everyone eats a little each hour, children first; cooked dishes are picked over raw food.
topics.long:
Food is ordinary items: potatoes, beans, meat, canned food, dishes from the kitchen. Each has a **food value** and a **nutrition** value. The breakdown below shows your stock against what the colony eats per day.

## Eating

- Everyone eats a little every hour; children and infants need less and are fed first.
- People prefer cooked dishes, better quality and variety, and eat what spoils soonest. Long-keeping food is saved for the road (see [[rations]]).
- With nothing to eat a survivor becomes **Hungry** and loses health every hour.
- Nutrition is averaged over a couple of days; a poor diet leads to Malnourished (see [[food_buffs]]).

## Getting food

- **Farm**: potatoes (ready in 1 day), herbs, beans (3 days), corn (4 days). Rain helps outdoor crops; dust storms bury them.
- **Greenhouse**: vegetables and herbs, indoors, whatever the weather.
- **Hunting Lodge**: game (meat and hides), Husk-zone game (plenty but tainted), forage.
- Switching a field's crop loses what is growing.

## Tips

- Keep several days of food in stock before a raid season or a long expedition.

topics.title: Spoilage and the Cold Cellar
topics.short: Food keeps for its shelf life, then spoils and rots away. A Cold Cellar slows fresh produce and meat to 60% (40% at level 2).
topics.long:
Every lot of food ages. Each item has a shelf life: potatoes about two weeks, beans a month, raw meat three days, Husk meat two, canned food half a year. Cooked dishes keep only a few days; preserved food keeps much longer.

## Spoiled food

- Past its shelf life a lot is **spoiled**: it no longer counts as food and is eaten only when nothing else is left, with a chance of food sickness.
- Two days later it rots away.

## The Cold Cellar

The **Cold Cellar** slows ageing for fresh produce and meat: they age at 60% of the normal rate, 40% at level 2. Preserved food does not need it.

## Keeping food longer

- Preserve: smoked and salted meat, pickles, dried food, canned and field rations.
- The Preserver perk makes a cook's preserved food keep longer.
- Raw meat cannot be eaten at all: cook it or preserve it before it turns.

## Tips

- Hunting brings meat that is gone in three days. Pair a Lodge with a cook.

topics.title: Cooking
topics.short: Campfire, Kitchen and Smokehouse turn raw food into dishes worth more mood, health and buffs. The cook's skill sets the dish's quality.
topics.long:
Cooking buildings work like any workshop: queue a recipe, and workers turn ingredients into dishes. The **Campfire** does simple food, the **Kitchen** (levels 1 to 3) meals, the **Smokehouse** preserves.

## Why cook

- Dishes are worth more food than their ingredients, add mood and health when eaten, and some give buffs: a stew or roast gives Well Fed, a pie Comfort Food (see [[food_buffs]]).
- A hot supper between dusk and dawn counts ×1.5 with a Campfire.
- Without a cooked meal for two days everyone gets Bland Diet.

## Quality

A dish rolls Crude, Standard or Fine from the cook's Cooking skill and the building level, like gear (see [[crafting]]). Crude dishes do ×0.8, Fine ×1.25. Tainted ingredients such as Husk meat stay tainted in a crude dish 60% of the time, 20% at Standard and never at Fine.

## For the road

Stew, pie, a feast or field rations of Standard quality or better give the party Fed for the Road: +1 AP on the first round in the field (see [[rations]]).

topics.title: Food buffs
topics.short: Meals leave buffs: Well Fed (+8% output, faster healing), Comfort Food, Energised. A poor diet gives Hungry, Bland, Malnourished or Same Again.
topics.long:
What people eat leaves a mark for hours afterwards. Buffs show as badges on survivor cards.

## Good

- **Well Fed** (roast, stew, feast): ×1.08 output, ×1.25 healing.
- **Comfort Food** (pie, feast): mood lifts every hour.
- **Energised** (stim tea): ×1.15 output, then a crash of 4 hours of sleep debt.
- **Soothed** (medicinal broth): ×1.5 healing and a little health every hour.
- **Fed for the Road** (stew, pie, feast, field rations): +1 AP on the first field round.

## Bad

- **Hungry** (went without food): ×0.85 output, ×0.75 healing.
- **Bland Diet** (no cooked meal for two days): mood drags.
- **Malnourished** (poor nutrition for days): ×0.9 output; children grow weaker.
- **Same Again** (one dish most days): mood drags.
- **Food Poisoning** (spoiled, raw or tainted food): ×0.75 output, losing mood and health, −1 AP on the first field round.

## Tips

- Vary the menu: two or three different dishes keep Same Again away.

topics.title: Health
topics.short: Health runs from 0 to 100. Low health cuts output by up to half; at 0 the survivor dies. Food, sleep and meals restore it.
topics.long:
Each survivor has health from 0 to 100, separate from the condition of each body part (see [[injuries]]).

## Why it matters

Job output is multiplied by a vitality factor from ×0.5 at 0 HP to ×1 at full health, on top of the body parts the job needs (see [[jobs_output]]). At 0 the survivor dies and joins the memorial.

## What restores it

- Every fed hour, a little.
- Sleep in a bed or a Med Bay cot.
- Dishes that heal, and the Soothed buff (see [[food_buffs]]).

## What drains it

- Starvation, every hour without food.
- Serious head and torso wounds left untreated.
- Infection from 75% severity, and Husk sickness (see [[infection]]).
- Working outdoors in a dust storm without a mask (it never takes health below 25).

## In the field

Hits do damage; a survivor at 0 is downed and starts to bleed out (see [[carry_downed]]).

topics.title: Injuries and fractures
topics.short: Wounds sit on body parts. Light ones heal on their own; serious ones get worse without care. A limb hit hard may break: splint it.
topics.long:
Damage lands on body parts (head, torso, arms, legs), each with a wound severity from 0 to 100%. A wounded part works worse, which costs output at jobs that use it and aim, movement or carrying in the field.

## How wounds change

- Under 30%: heals slowly on its own.
- 60% or more: gets **worse** without Med Bay care. A limb that reaches 100% is lost; head and torso wounds drain health.
- At the [[med_bay]] every wound heals, faster with good medics and Medicine.

## Fractures

When a hit leaves an arm or leg at 45% or worse there is a 35% chance it breaks: −25% efficiency and half-speed healing. A **splint** cuts the penalty to −8% and makes it heal ×1.25.

## Pain

A worst wound of 55% or more costs 15% output until a painkiller dulls it. Three painkillers close together start a dependency.

## Dressings

A bandage lowers the chance a wound gets infected; a clean dressing stops it. A new injury undoes the dressing (see [[infection]]).

## Tips

- A lost limb can be replaced (see [[prosthetic_tiers]]).

topics.title: Infection and sickness
topics.short: Undressed wounds can turn infected: fever, no healing and later health loss. Dress wounds, use antibiotics. Bad food brings sickness.
topics.long:
## Wound infection

- A **dirty wound** of 25% or more has a small chance each hour to go bad. A bandage cuts the chance to about a third, a clean dressing to nothing, and a Med Bay bed halves it.
- An infection starts mild and grows over about a week. It stops that part healing and brings **fever**: up to −35% output.
- From 50% it costs 1 AP in the field; from 75% it drains health, and it can kill.
- **Antibiotics** cure it. A patient at the Med Bay on Medicine holds it back.
- A failed surgery leaves a surgical infection that works the same way.

## Sickness

- **Food sickness** (spoiled, raw or bad food): −30% output, passes in a day or two. Rest at the Med Bay speeds it.
- **Husk sickness** (tainted Husk meat): −45% output, drags on and drains health. It can kill.
- An **antidote** cures either at once.

## Tips

- The Med Bay treats infections second, right after bleeding (see [[med_bay]]).
- Keep sick survivors home: fever costs AP in the field.

topics.title: Medical supplies
topics.short: Bandages, splints, antiseptic, antibiotics, painkillers, blood bags and more, made at the Med Bay. Quality changes how well they work.
topics.long:
**Medicine** is a stockpile resource the Med Bay uses for its patients. **Medical supplies** are items you make at the Med Bay and carry into the field.

## The supplies

- Open from the start: bandage, splint, herbal remedy, antiseptic and the basic med-kit.
- Found or learned from schematics: antibiotics, painkillers, antidote, clean dressings, blood bags, stims, suture and surgical kits, and the Linked "Calm" injector.
- Each rolls Crude, Standard or Fine from the medic's Medicine skill: Crude works at ×0.8, Fine at ×1.25.

## At home

The Med Bay treats its patients from your stock in priority order: bleeding, infection, fracture, sickness, pain. Reorder or switch these off in the dispensary. It never gives painkillers to someone close to dependency. You can treat anyone at home yourself from their Body tab.

## In the field

- Items are on keys 4–9.
- A med-kit gets a downed ally up with 15 HP, a field trauma kit with 30, a blood bag with 45. Making a blood bag needs a donor with 70+ health.
- A stim gives 1 AP now and takes 1 next round. The Calm injector stops suppression pinning you, at a cost in [[humanity]].

topics.title: Med Bay
topics.short: Patients heal here: beds by level, medics speed it up, and each patient uses Medicine. Surgery for prosthetics happens here too.
topics.long:
The **Med Bay** holds 2, 3 or 5 patients by level and has room for 1 or 2 medics.

## Care

- Admitted patients do not work; they go home once healed. The sick and infected are admitted too.
- Every hour each wound heals by a rate set by the Med Bay's level, times the care given: an unstaffed bay gives 40% care, and each medic adds their own performance at the Medicine job (see [[jobs_output]]).
- Each patient uses a little **Medicine** every hour. Without it, patients heal only at the natural rate (but do not get worse).
- Medics train Medicine only while someone is in a bed.

## Treatments and surgery

- The bay treats patients from your supplies (see [[medicine]]).
- Prosthetics above the basic ones go on by surgery here (see [[prosthetic_tiers]]). A level 3 bay on power adds +5% to surgery success.

## Tips

- Keep Medicine in stock: a patient without it only heals what would heal anyway.
- The Well Fed and Soothed buffs speed healing (see [[food_buffs]]).
